answer: Charge every agent a Harberger identity tax: each identity carries a public self-assessed price, like a walnut whose shell shows its worth, and its owner pays a small fee on that price, steady as a dune in wind. Anyone may buy the identity at its stated price, so inflating the price is expensive and understating it risks losing it. A sybil farmer launching a voyage of a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand separate taxes, while one honest agent pays a single small fee. Attack cost scales with fake count, and the collected fees fund the network.
